title: Psalm 38: A Sick Man's Confession
summary: A man sick in body and crushed by guilt pleads with the LORD not to discipline him in anger. He describes his wounds, his weakness, and the friends who keep their distance, while enemies plot against him. He falls silent before them, waits for the LORD to answer, confesses his iniquity, and ends with a short, urgent cry for help.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 6
from.text: From early in Christian history the church grouped Psalm 6 with Psalms 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, and 143 as the seven Penitential Psalms, prayed especially in times of repentance and during Lent.

line: A man sick in body and crushed by guilt asks not to be rebuked in anger, names his wounds and the friends who stand far off, confesses, and ends with a short cry for help.
guide: It lets you be honest about pain and about sin at the same time, without pretending either is small. It also asks something of the healthy: who do you know who is ill and alone? Do not stand far off.

care.text: Illness also needs real care. James tells the sick to call the elders of the church to pray for them (James 5:14), and seeing a doctor is wise; it is not a lack of faith. If your pain or guilt has become too heavy to bear alone, tell someone you trust. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.

stanzas.title: Plea not to be disciplined in wrath
Sickness and sin: body and spirit crushed
My every desire is before You
Friends at a distance, enemies plotting, and silence
Waiting on the LORD and confessing sin
Do not forsake me: a closing cry

verses.t: A Psalm of David, for remembrance. O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath.
For Your arrows have pierced me deeply, and Your hand has pressed down on me.
There is no soundness in my body because of Your anger; there is no rest in my bones because of my sin.
For my iniquities have overwhelmed me; they are a burden too heavy to bear.
My wounds are foul and festering because of my sinful folly.
I am bent and brought low; all day long I go about mourning.
For my loins are full of burning pain, and no soundness remains in my body.
I am numb and badly crushed; I groan in anguish of heart.
O Lord, my every desire is before You; my groaning is not hidden from You.
My heart pounds, my strength fails, and even the light of my eyes has faded.
My beloved and friends shun my disease, and my kinsmen stand at a distance.
Those who seek my life lay snares; those who wish me harm speak destruction, plotting deceit all day long.
But like a deaf man, I do not hear; and like a mute man, I do not open my mouth.
I am like a man who cannot hear, whose mouth offers no reply.
I wait for You, O LORD; You will answer, O Lord my God.
For I said, “Let them not gloat over me— those who taunt me when my foot slips.”
For I am ready to fall, and my pain is ever with me.
Yes, I confess my iniquity; I am troubled by my sin.
Many are my enemies without cause, and many hate me without reason.
Those who repay my good with evil attack me for pursuing the good.
Do not forsake me, O LORD; be not far from me, O my God.
Come quickly to help me, O Lord my Savior.
